title: Letter 30 — On Temptations and Patience
attribution_note: Letter 30 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: Temptations for those who turn to God

pairs.en: I have heard your complaint concerning your troubles, and upon this, according to my poor understanding, I offer you counsel.

Those who have turned to God always meet with many temptations, of which Scripture also writes thus: *“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.* *Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble,”* and the rest. [Sirach 2:1–2] And in many places of Holy Scripture the same is witnessed.

Therefore one must endure, and arm oneself against them with prayer, and so overcome them. Satan sleepeth not, but is always watchful for our destruction, according to the apostolic teaching: *“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour: whom resist stedfast in the faith,”* and the rest. [1 Peter 5:8–9] The apostle James says: *“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.”* [James 1:12]
Therefore endure, and wait for mercy from God, and for the end in the age to come.

When thoughts pull you back to your former life and into vanity, beware of this. This is a snare of Satan: he would seduce you, entangle you in vanity, and so destroy you. Hear Holy Scripture concerning this: *“No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God,”* says Christ. [Luke 9:62] And the apostle Peter says: *“It had been better for them”* — that is, for those who return to a lawless life — *“not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them.* *But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.”* [2 Peter 2:21–22]

And in the hundred and twenty-fourth psalm, in the fifth verse, it is written: *“As for such as turn aside unto their crooked ways, the Lord shall lead them forth with the workers of iniquity.”* [Psalm 124:5] And Christ again says: *“For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?”* [Matthew 16:26]

Everything here will remain: the world, riches, glory, honour, luxury, carnal pleasure, ornaments, garments, houses, adornments, horses, carriages, vessels, carnal food, fullness — all will pass away; death will come, and will snatch us away naked, and send us into that world. Woe will it be to us if it snatches us away, seduced by vanity, burdened with sins, and naked of virtues!

How shall we appear at the Judgment of Christ? Shame and everlasting disgrace there will be; the whole world will see our nakedness. The saints of God will not know us, if we do not imitate them here. The holy angels will abhor us, because we were called Christians, yet were not Christians — that is, we had not a Christian life. Christ will say: *“I never knew you”* [Matthew 7:23]! “Ye knew Me not, and kept not My commandments, and followed Me not in humility, love, meekness and patience while ye lived in the world — and I know you not now.”
O God, suffer us not to hear this voice!

Therefore let us endure a little, that we may be comforted forever. Behold, soon, soon all will pass away! Behold, *He that shall come will come, and will not tarry.* [Hebrews 10:37] Behold, soon there will be a change: for them that endure — eternal consolation; but for them that take comfort here in the sweets and merriments and lusts of this world — eternal sorrow, straitness and anguish.
Be saved! May the Lord strengthen you, and have mercy on me, a sinner. Amen.
